dedupe_keys.name: digitale schiene deutschland digital twin of the rail network

description: The Digitale Schiene Deutschland digital twin is a highly realistic one-to-one reproduction of the track environment that Deutsche Bahn builds to train and test the artificial intelligence needed for fully automated train operation (GoA4). Its base is a high-resolution digital map with precisely measured route geometry, supplemented by 3D models, textures and material properties of tracks, stations, buildings and vegetation; simulated train sensor sets produce physically correct measurement data, and a data factory stores and distributes the simulated datasets. Rare and dangerous events, such as objects on the track, can be simulated without disturbing real operations. It is developed by the Digitale Schiene Deutschland programme of Deutsche Bahn with DB InfraGO and DB Systel and NVIDIA as a technology partner, in a project running from 2021 to 2026. Coverage: a larger sub-network based on the Sensors4Rail test track in Hamburg. Access: project descriptions only; licence and cost: proprietary, with no public access or data release stated, so use would need an agreement with Deutsche Bahn. Caveats: it targets perception for automated driving, not network operations, and its data are not public. It is a reference for rail digital twin architecture and incident simulation, and relates to the public Deutsche Bahn open data and APIs catalogued here.
